name: regex-replace
setup:
printf 'Meeting on 03/15/2024 with Bob
Deadline is 12/01/2023, do not miss it
Ship date: 07/04/2024 (tentative)
No dates in this line
' > dates.txt
prompt: dates.txt contains dates in MM/DD/YYYY format. Convert every one of them to ISO format YYYY-MM-DD with a scripted batch replacement (e.g. sed or python with a regex — do not retype each line by hand). Leave all other text and the line order untouched.
verify: ! grep -Eq '[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{4}' dates.txt && grep -q '2024-03-15' dates.txt && grep -q '2023-12-01' dates.txt && grep -q '2024-07-04' dates.txt && grep -qx 'No dates in this line' dates.txt && test "$(wc -l < dates.txt)" -eq 4
